CH.coreZoneText: Danger level "considerable" (3=) in northwest to northeast to southeast facing aspects above 2600m.

avalancheProblems.comment:
The fresh snow and in particular the wind slabs that are being formed by the sometimes strong westerly wind are prone to triggering. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches. Dry avalanches can additionally be released in the old snowpack in particular on very steep north facing slopes. These can reach large size. Ski touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

weatherForecast.comment:

The night will be rather cloudy. On Ascension Day it will be quite sunny along the Main Alpine Ridge in Upper Valais and in the Gotthard region, while elsewhere it will be very cloudy. Precipitation will be encountered over a wide area. The snowfall level will be between 1300 m in the north and 1800 m in the south.

Fresh snow

  • Extreme west of Lower Valais, Vaud and Fribourg Alps: 20 to 30 cm
  • Other regions of Lower Valais and the northern flank of the Alps, Val Bregaglia and the Bernina region: 10 to 20 cm
  • Less elsewhere

Temperature

At midday at 2000 m, between -3 °C in the north and +1 °C in the south

Wind

Southwesterly to westerly

It will be very cloudy, with around 10 cm of snow falling over a wide area, less in Upper Valais and Ticino. The snowfall level will be around 1300 m. The wind will be mostly light.

The avalanche danger will not change significantly.

There will be a widespread increase in avalanche risk. In Upper Valais and Ticino, it will not change significantly.

CH.coreZoneText: Danger level "moderate" (2+) in northwest to northeast to east facing aspects above 2600m.

avalancheProblems.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and northwesterly wind, wind slabs formed at elevated altitudes. These are only small but can in some cases be released easily. They are to be evaluated with care and prudence in extreme terrain.
Additionally avalanches can also be released in near-surface layers and reach medium size. These avalanche prone locations are rather rare but are barely recognisable. Careful route selection is recommended.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

As a consequence of a sometimes storm force northwesterly wind, wind slabs formed on Tuesday in particular in gullies and bowls and behind abrupt changes in the terrain. These are rather small but in some cases prone to triggering. They are to be evaluated with care and prudence in steep terrain. Apart from the danger of being buried, restraint should be exercised as well in view of the danger of avalanches sweeping people along and giving rise to falls.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
